verdict.rationale: Glama is an MCP gateway and hosting platform, so per-end-user credential isolation is a fair question for it. The evidence shows only generic gateway credential management ('credential-managed') and per-tool access control, which are adjacent features. Nothing documents separate connected accounts or scoped tokens per end user of a customer's product. The account-bound ownership token is for verifying server ownership, a different capability.

support.subject: As a platform-engineer, I can maintain separate connected accounts and scoped tokens per end user of my product, so each user's agent acts only on that user's credentials
